messages.subject: example with a loop
messages.body_plain:
Dear Developers,

So far the simmer package has worked for the codes that I have created. However, the next example I am trying to create involves cycling clients to the system. What I am looking for is a trajectory that has an arrival of new clients to one resource. After being serviced, they will return at the start of the process and undergo the same trajectory again. The resource thus has two types of clients entering: new ones and cycled ones. The options I considered are having two streams of clients, using attributes, recursive code or time stamps. All of these have their own issues. Do you have any suggestions on how to model such a system in simmer?

regards, A.

messages.subject: Re: [simmer-devel] example with a loop
messages.body_plain:
Hi Iñaki,

thank you for the suggestion. Rollback seems to work.
Here is an example code for whoever wants to try.

traj <- trajectory("patients") %>%
    ## State called "resource".
    seize(., "doctor", amount=1) %>%
    timeout(2.1) %>%
    release( "doctor", amount=1) %>%
    ## Go back to the beginning (seize) twice in a row.
    rollback(3, times=2);

env <- simmer() %>%
    add_resource("doctor", capacity=Inf) %>%
    add_generator("patient", traj, function() 3) %>%
run(until=10)

get_mon_resources(env, data=c("counts", "limits"));
get_mon_arrivals(env, ongoing=TRUE);

A.
